title: One simulated AMD purchase; the other active book kept its cash
body_html:
One simulated AMD purchase; the other active book kept its cash

Paper trading · 2026-11-10T17:00:23.981848-05:00

The cutoff is 2026-11-10 22:00:23.981 UTC (17:00:23 Eastern). The paper account snapshot showed $2,000 cash and equity, with no broker fill recorded in the supplied records. Of the two books evaluated today, mean-reversion recorded a deliberate wait and no proposal; short-horizon proposed AMD, received deterministic approval, and recorded a simulated fill. The cutoff book marks are snapshot-based: MU was observed at 21:45:32.976 UTC and AMD at 21:00:00.022 UTC. These are not guaranteed closing prices or live quotes. Older snapshots can precede a day's fills, so their timing matters when reading performance.

Today's lesson: An approved proposal is not yet a fill

Approval and execution are separate events. The AMD proposal passed deterministic risk, then a simulated fill record confirmed a book purchase of 0.097068 shares at $513.98. The same book's later $513.69 midpoint is $0.29 lower per share, making the supplied unrealized loss about $0.03. That mark is a recorded snapshot and excludes fees.

Portfolio review

Paper account

The paper account snapshot at 2026-11-10 22:00:23.368 UTC shows $2,000 cash and $2,000 equity. The run-start performance record at 20:15:40 UTC also showed $2,000 equity, with reported P&L and return of zero. No broker fill record appears in the supplied day's records. The AMD fill described elsewhere belongs to a simulated book and is not a paper-account fill. No account-level paper thesis or counterargument is recorded, so the separate book decisions should not be treated as paper-account decisions.

mean-reversion

At the cutoff, this book had $1,950.01 cash and marked equity of $1,990.99, compared with $2,000 starting cash. That is about $9.01 below starting cash on the recorded mark; realized P&L is $0 and the MU holding's supplied unrealized loss is $9.01. The mark combines cash replay with the MU observation at 21:45:32.976 UTC, so it is a snapshot-based book mark, not live equity. The completed evaluation recorded a deliberate wait on a new SNDK position and no proposals, approvals, or fills. Its recorded counterargument was that SNDK's low trailing earnings multiple and reported cash-flow yield could offer an opportunity if unusually high profits persist; the decision judged that margin normalization remained a credible risk. A separate SPY buy-and-hold reference failed because its quote postdated the valuation cutoff; that failed reference supplies no comparison result and was not the book decision.

mean-reversion-adversary

This book is marked paused. Its cutoff record shows $2,000 cash, $2,000 marked equity, and $0 realized P&L, against $2,000 starting cash. No holding details for this book are supplied, and the day's book-run summary includes no evaluation, proposal, approval, or fill for it. That means there is no day's decision or performance change to explain from these records; the supplied data also contains no recorded counterargument for this book.

short-horizon

At the cutoff, the book had $1,950.11 cash and marked equity of $1,999.97, compared with $2,000 starting cash. The roughly 3-cent difference is the supplied unrealized loss on AMD; realized P&L is $0. The book proposed a $50 AMD limit purchase with a maximum price of $515.10. Deterministic risk approved it, and a simulated fill record shows 0.097068 shares bought at $513.98. Approval alone would not prove a fill; this simulated fill record does. It is not a broker fill. The later book valuation used an AMD midpoint observation at 21:00:00 UTC, after the simulated fill at 20:38:32 UTC. The strongest recorded counterargument was that one recovery session and an unfinished snapshot might prove to be a failed bounce, while broader momentum remained negative and the quote was wide.

Every holding

MU — mean-reversion

The book holds 0.053191 MU shares at an average purchase price of $939.88 per share. Its observed midpoint was $770.53 at 2026-11-10 21:45:32.976 UTC; the marked value is $40.99 and the supplied unrealized loss is $9.01. For example, the observed price is $169.35 below the average purchase price, multiplied across this small shareholding. Book purchase prices and gains exclude fees. The cutoff valuation uses this recorded observation, not a guaranteed closing or live price. The day's mean-reversion decision said to keep the existing MU holding unchanged. Its available reasoning points to profitability and cash generation, while noting that MU's 74.59% operating margin is at a retained historical maximum versus a 22.59% median. The decision also says the original holding rationale and invalidation conditions are incomplete in the available historical record. That missing context limits confidence about the original thesis; the strongest recorded counterargument is that unusually high margins may not persist, alongside recent price weakness. No new MU proposal or fill is recorded today.

Source records86269a23-1f1c-4bf8-8088-20be7a50479b:MU, 541884d3-a186-46c6-b07d-72f6df11b4c6

AMD — short-horizon

The book holds 0.097068 AMD shares at an average purchase price of $513.98 per share. The observed midpoint was $513.69 at 2026-11-10 21:00:00.022 UTC. The marked value is $49.86 and the supplied unrealized loss is about $0.03: the midpoint is $0.29 below the average purchase price, or roughly 2.8 cents across these shares. Book purchase prices and gains exclude fees. The recorded reasoning was a small, short-horizon test of price recovery, with company-news context; it described the November 10 evidence as partial follow-through, not a confirmed full-session breakout. The strongest counterargument is that the move could be a failed bounce within a broader downtrend, with a wide quote and mixed news. The observed price is a snapshot, not a guaranteed closing or live price.

Decision, approval, fill, and failure are different records

The mean-reversion book's evaluation completed and recorded a deliberate wait. Separately, its SPY buy-and-hold reference failed because the quote postdated the valuation cutoff. That reference failure is not a trade decision or evidence of deliberate waiting. In short-horizon, a completed evaluation proposed and filled a simulated AMD purchase. The run summary reports no rejected proposals.

Read a book mark as cash plus observed holdings

For short-horizon, $1,950.11 cash plus $49.86 marked AMD value gives $1,999.97 book equity. The small gap from the $2,000 starting cash matches the supplied AMD unrealized loss of about $0.03. For mean-reversion, $1,950.01 cash plus $40.99 marked MU value gives $1,990.99. These book gains exclude fees and use the recorded price observations.

What to watch next

The short-horizon decision record called for reviewing AMD on November 11: check whether completed-session evidence sustains the recovery and compare it with the stated failure conditions. The mean-reversion decision named SNDK's next quarterly results as a point to reassess its earnings durability. These are recorded review points, not guarantees about what the next data will show.

Observed midpoint: A recorded price observation used to estimate a holding's value. It may be older than the report cutoff and is not necessarily a closing or live price.

Simulated fill: A fill recorded inside a simulated book. It does not mean a broker executed an order.

Deterministic risk: A rule-based check that approves or rejects a proposal. Approval does not by itself mean an order filled.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
